items.note: The standing setting of the chapter (lines 36-40): F : Vec n → ℝ with ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ F (finite and convex); "F_* = min F attained" is IsLeast (Set.range F) Fstar, unfolded by min_attained_iff to (∃ x, F x = Fstar) ∧ ∀ x, Fstar ≤ F x; K is a variable with hK_def : K = {x | F x ≤ b}, hb : b > Fstar, hK : IsCompact K in every theorem of the module that uses the setting.

With line 40 ("Ordinary full BFGS uses differentiable accepted endpoints"): every admissible run satisfies g_k = ∇F(x_k) (HasFDerivAt F (gradientFunctional (R.g k)) (R.x k)), s_k = -α_kH_kg_k (R.displacement k), x_{k+1} = x_k + s_k, y_k = g_{k+1} - g_k (R.gradientChange k) (run_display); admissible_iff shows that the structure AdmissibleBFGSRun is exactly the definition of an admissible run.

H_0 ≻ 0, α_k > 0 and the inverse update H_{k+1} = (I - s_ky_kᵀ/t_k)H_k(I - y_ks_kᵀ/t_k) + s_ks_kᵀ/t_k with t_k = y_kᵀs_k = R.curvature k (update_display); t_k > 0 along every run, so (t_k)⁻¹ is 1/t_k.
The fields armijo and weak_wolfe of AdmissibleBFGSRun, with fixed constants 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1 (R.c₁, R.c₂); both inequalities non-strict (line_search_display).

With line 57: for differentiable x, z with gradients g, h (HasFDerivAt F (gradientFunctional g) x, ... h z), y = h - g, s = z - x. The library pair quantities are pairStep x z = z - x, pairDecrease x z g = -gᵀ(z - x), pairCurvature x z g h = (h - g)ᵀ(z - x) (pair_notation, rfl).
d = -gᵀs = pairDecrease x z g, t = yᵀs = pairCurvature x z g h; Δ = F(x) - F(z) is written out (eligible_iff takes d, Δ, t as variables with these defining equations).
EligiblePair F c₁ c₂ x z g h is exactly: x, z differentiable with gradients g, h, d > 0, c₁d ≤ Δ ≤ d and t ≥ (1 - c₂)d (eligible_iff, with s, y, d, Δ, t as variables with their defining equations).

With line 70 ("For s≠0, define the Euclidean orthogonal projector"): stepProjector s = 1 - (sᵀs)⁻¹ • outer s s; for s ≠ 0 it is symmetric, idempotent, Π_s s = 0 and Π_s v = v for vᵀs = 0, i.e. the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto s^⊥ (projector_display).

items.title: One-sided transported-certificate convergence
items.note: Setting of lines 36-39 (IsLeast (Set.range F) Fstar, K = {F ≤ b} compact, b > Fstar; convexity is part of the run). The certificate hypothesis is written out in the statement: for each η > 0 with K_η = {x | x ∈ K ∧ F x ≥ Fstar + η} nonempty, ∃ W : Vec n → Mat n (finite-valued) and m > 0, C (any real: C_η < ∞), L ≥ 0, δ > 0 with W(x) PSD (symmetric) at differentiable points of K_η, (V) gᵀW(x)g ≥ m at every differentiable x ∈ K_η with g = ∇F(x), and (S), (T) for eligible pairs x, z ∈ K_η (for the run's constants R.c₁, R.c₂) with d = -gᵀ(z - x) ≤ δ; A ⪯ B is (B - A).PosSemidef. Conclusions: F(x_k) → F_*, Euclidean dist(x_k, argmin F) → 0 (euclideanSolutionDistance), and x_k → x_* when x_* is the unique minimizer. hasBandCertificates_iff/bandCertificate_iff show the hypothesis is the library's HasBandCertificates; the library theorem is transportedCertificateConvergence (no sign condition on C, as in the companion; the article's Definition art:band-certificate asks C ≥ 0).
B_k = R.hessian k = (R.H k)⁻¹, q_k = R.q k = g_kᵀH_kg_k, d_k = R.d k = α_kq_k (proof_notation, rfl).
(3.3), stated under the hypotheses of the theorem (certificate hypothesis as HasBandCertificates, unused ones prefixed _), for every k.
M_k is the variable M k with hM : M k = R.hessian k - (R.q k)⁻¹ • outer (R.g k) (R.g k); (M k).PosSemidef. "by metric Cauchy–Schwarz" is the proof method (the library proof).
(3.4): M_ks_k = 0 and M_k = Π_{s_k}M_kΠ_{s_k}, with s_k = R.displacement k.

(3.5) under the hypotheses of the theorem: (1/N)∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ → ∞. The run stays in K, so gradients are bounded and ∑ d_k < ∞ (run_bounds), and Chapter M's Theorem M:average (article Theorem art:reciprocal-growth, library objectiveReciprocalGrowth) applies.

Standing assumptions of the reductio (line 144): the theorem's hypotheses, Tendsto (F(x_k) - Fstar) → ℓ with ℓ > 0, the certificate Cert of K_{ℓ/2} ("Use the field for η=ℓ/2"), k₀ with d_k ≤ Cert.δ for k ≥ k₀; E and a are variables with E k = tr(B_k W(x_k)), a k = 1 + L d_k. Claim: E_k ≥ 0 for k ≥ k₀. tail_exists proves that such k₀ exists and that the tail pairs lie in the band. General form with satisfiable assumptions: the article's certificate_energy_nonneg (x_k in a band). These reductio assumptions are jointly inconsistent (the theorem shows the gap tends to 0).

(3.6), all four lines (two equalities, two inequalities) for every k ≥ k₀, under the standing assumptions of disp/018 and M_k of disp/015; C may be any real. The reductio assumptions are inconsistent; the proof uses trace_step_general, whose assumptions (a certificate on some band, x_k, x_{k+1} in the band, d_k ≤ δ) are satisfiable (examples at the end of the module). The lead-in (line 148) cites (3.3)-(3.4) as "(3)--(4)": a typo, recorded as prose/042 (the display itself is correct).

P is a variable with P k₀ = 1 and P (k+1) = P k * a k for k ≥ k₀; Pbar = exp(L ∑_{j≥0} d_{k₀+j}) (a real number, so Pbar < ∞). Claim: 1 ≤ P_k ≤ Pbar for k ≥ k₀. General form: the article's normalization_bounds (only L ≥ 0 and ∑ d_k < ∞).

For every N ≥ k₀: (m/Pbar)∑_{k=k₀}^{N-1} q_k⁻¹ ≤ E_{k₀} + C(N - k₀). The companion allows any real C_η; the derivation of the display needs C ≥ 0, which holds here because (S) applies to the accepted pair (x_{k₀}, x_{k₀+1}) in the band (C_nonneg_of_pair: 0 ≤ yᵀW(z)y ≤ Ct with t > 0). General form with satisfiable assumptions: the article's certificate_budget_general. The lead-in "Divide (6) by P_{k+1} and sum" (line 160) means (3.6), and "This contradicts (5)" (line 165) means (3.5): typos, recorded as prose/042 (the display itself is correct).

With lines 174-176: for finite convex F with unique minimizer x_* (F_* = F(x_*)), compact sublevel K and U ∈ 𝓝 x_*, ∃ c > F_* with F(x) ≥ c on K \ U (so inf_{K∖U} F > F_*, the infimum of the empty set being +∞). The proof gives c = F_* + δ with {F ≤ F_* + δ} ⊆ U.

For all v(x), v(z), s, λ, β, L, d: v(z) = λv(x) + βs and |λ|² ≤ 1 + Ld imply Π_s v(z)v(z)ᵀ Π_s ⪯ (1 + Ld) Π_s v(x)v(x)ᵀ Π_s, i.e. (T) for W = vvᵀ. rank_one_certificate assembles the band certificate with W = vvᵀ from the scalar conditions.

gᵀ(vvᵀ)g = |gᵀv|², yᵀ(vvᵀ)y = |yᵀv|² (rank_one_conditions), so (V), (S) for W = vvᵀ are the displayed scalar conditions; rank_one_certificate: these and the sufficient transport of disp/023 give a BandCertificate with W = vvᵀ and the same m, C, L, δ. Wording point W17 applied on 15 October 2026: the lead-in (line 192) reads "Conditions (V) and (S) become" (before "Conditions (V)--(S) become", a range of condition names).

The radial field W(x) = (x - x_*)(x - x_*)ᵀ is outer (x - xstar) (x - xstar); its quadratic form is aᵀW(x)a = (aᵀ(x - x_*))² (radial_field_energy). "Given (RS)": the radial secant condition of Chapter R (04_R.tex:53-59; printed with C_η ≥ 0 since W19, equivalent to real constants by Ch04R.RSNonneg_iff) is the library's HasRadialSecantBounds with real constants (rs_iff, Iff.rfl). Wording point W18 applied on 15 October 2026: line 217 reads "Given the radial secant condition (RS) of Chapter~\ref{comp:R}, take" (before "Given (RS), take", with no pointer to the definition (4.RS), 04_R.tex:53-59). Since 15 October 2026 Chapter 4 also gives the condition this name (04_R.tex:53, wording point W8, C/04_R/prose/006).

Setting of the section: F finite convex with minimizer x_*, F_* = F(x_*), K = {F ≤ b} compact, (RS) on K (unused, _hRS). For every differentiable x ∈ K_η with g = ∇F(x): gᵀW(x)g = (gᵀ(x - x_*))² ≥ (F(x) - F_*)² ≥ η².
Π_s(z - x_*) = Π_s(x - x_*) with s = z - x, for all x, z, x_* (an algebraic identity; the (RS) context of the paragraph is not needed).
With line 233: for symmetric W(x), W(z) (in the theorem W is PSD, hence symmetric, at the differentiable endpoints of eligible pairs), (T) ⇔ aᵀW(z)a ≤ (1 + Ld)aᵀW(x)a for every a with aᵀs = 0.

items.anchor: The reciprocal budget becomes an objective theorem only when geometry controls a comparison energy.
items.reason: Motivation of the chapter, about the proof method: the reciprocal budget of Chapter M is turned into a convergence theorem through control of a comparison energy (theorem/001). "only when" describes this route, not a necessary condition for convergence of BFGS (the certificate is not necessary: the article's certificate_not_necessary).

items.anchor: Visibility, secant control and transport are imposed on objective-level pairs, not inferred from a presumed limit of the BFGS matrices.
items.note: Describes the hypotheses of theorem/001: (V), (S), (T) are conditions on F, the bands K_η and eligible pairs (objective data); one_sided_convergence assumes nothing about the matrices H_k or their limits.

items.anchor: An infinite admissible run has nonzero gradients and well-defined accepted steps.
items.note: The infinite-admissible-run convention (01_I.tex:40-47) is the structure AdmissibleBFGSRun (admissible_iff). admissible_run_def: g_k ≠ 0, s_k ≠ 0, t_k > 0 (so the update is well defined) and H_k ≻ 0 for every k.

items.anchor: These are the algorithmic quantifiers in Xie--W\"achter~\cite{XW}.
items.reason: Literature attribution (the conventions of Xie–Wächter); no mathematical claim.

items.anchor: No particular line-search implementation, damping, restart, or proximal operation is added.
items.reason: Scope of the algorithm: the run model (AdmissibleBFGSRun) fixes the full BFGS update and the two line-search inequalities and specifies no implementation, damping, restart or proximal step; nothing to prove.

items.anchor: Every accepted step is eligible.
items.note: For every admissible run and k, (x_k, x_{k+1}) with gradients (g_k, g_{k+1}) is eligible for the run's constants, with d = d_k and t = t_k.

items.anchor: The upper bound $\Delta\le d$ follows from convexity.
items.note: F(x) - F(z) ≤ -gᵀ(z - x) for finite convex F, differentiable x with g = ∇F(x), and every z.

items.anchor: Eligibility does not assert compatibility of an arbitrary chain with BFGS
items.reason: Scope remark: EligiblePair F c₁ c₂ x z g h is a property of one pair, defined from F and the constants; the clause disclaims that chains of eligible pairs are realizable by BFGS. Nothing to prove. The second clause of the sentence ("imposing a condition on all such pairs is an objective-only sufficient assumption") is prose/044.

items.anchor: All matrices in the next assumption are objective-pair data, not $H_k$.
items.note: Clarifies the hypothesis of theorem/001: the field W_η and the constants are chosen per band, from F alone, before and independently of the run (∀ η ... ∃ W m C L δ in one_sided_convergence).

items.anchor: Condition (V) says that the comparison directions retain a nonzero component of the gradient on a positive band.
items.note: The three readings made precise: (V) with m > 0 forces W(x)g ≠ 0 (g has a nonzero component in the range of the PSD W); for t > 0, (S) is exactly yᵀW(z)y/t ≤ C, the bound on the secant correction term of (3.6); for symmetric W(x), W(z), (T) is exactly the comparison on vectors a with aᵀs = 0.

items.anchor: There is no uniform positive-definiteness requirement on $W_\eta$.
items.note: Remark on the hypotheses of theorem/001: only W_η(x) ⪰ 0 at differentiable band points is required (no positive definiteness, uniform or not).

items.anchor: Uniform boundedness of $W_\eta$ is convenient in examples but is not used by the proof; it is enough that its values are finite.
items.note: Remark on the hypotheses of theorem/001: the field is any W : Vec n → Mat n (real, i.e. finite, entries) with no bound; one_sided_convergence assumes none.

items.anchor: Constants and the field may depend on the positive band and the fixed line-search parameters.
items.note: Restates the quantifier order of theorem/001: for each η a field and constants (∀ η ∃ W m C L δ), and eligibility uses the run's fixed c₁, c₂; nothing is required uniformly in η, so they may degenerate as η ↓ 0.

items.anchor: \subsection{Proof}
items.note: The proof of theorem/001 is a subsection ending with \qed, so the extractor has no proof item for it; this item records it. Its displays disp/013-disp/021 are items; undisplayed general facts are prose/015 and prose/016; tail_exists states the tail of line 144. Its equation references (3.3)-(3.4) (line 148), (3.6) (line 160) and (3.5) (line 165) printed "(3)--(4)", "(6)" and "(5)" until their correction on 15 October 2026 (M25, item prose/042); the proof is correct.

items.anchor: Armijo implies $\sum d_k<\infty$.
items.note: A general fact used in the proof: for an admissible run with values bounded below (here by F_*), ∑ d_k < ∞.

items.anchor: a finite convex function has uniformly bounded subgradients on a compact set
items.note: Standard fact stated in the proof: for finite convex F and compact K, ∃ G with ‖g‖ ≤ G (Euclidean) for every x ∈ K and every subgradient g at x. "as follows by comparing its values at x and x+εu on a slightly enlarged compact set" is the proof method (as in the library proof of convex_supporting_bound_on_compact). run_bounds applies it to the run.

items.anchor: The formal principal theorem uses the same derived trace recurrence with a harmless larger additive bound $C_+(k+1)$
items.note: Mathematical content: (3.6) implies E_{k+1} ≤ (1 + Ld_k)(E_k - m/q_k) + C_+(k+1), C_+ = max{C, 0}, whenever x_k, x_{k+1} ∈ K_η and d_k ≤ δ. That the formal principal theorem uses it describes the Lean library (band_certificate_incompatible).

items.anchor: The normalized energy estimate then gives an $O(N^2)$ reciprocal-sum bound and contradicts
items.note: quadratic_budget: if a whole run lies in one band with d_k ≤ δ and ∑ d_k < ∞, then (m/exp(∑ L d_k))∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ ≤ E_0 + C_+N(N+1)/2 (O(N²)), and with bounded gradients this contradicts Chapter M's Theorem M:superquadratic (superquadratic_growth). Those hypotheses are the reductio's; quadratic_budget_finite (x_k in the band for k ≤ N) has satisfiable hypotheses (example at the end).

items.anchor: Its additional summability requirement is already a consequence of Armijo and the finite limiting value.
items.note: If F(x_k) has a finite limit then ∑ d_k < ∞.

items.anchor: Thus no extra hypothesis is added.
items.reason: Statement about the Lean formalization (the formal theorem transportedCertificateConvergence has no hypothesis beyond those of theorem/001; its summability input is derived, prose/019); software description.

items.anchor: The sharper linear telescoping estimate above follows from the separately proved scalar transport budget
items.note: The linear estimate (disp/021 form, (m/exp(∑ L d_k))∑_{k<N} q_k⁻¹ ≤ E_0 + CN for a run inside one band) derived from the scalar budget ScalarTransport.reciprocal_sum_le (linear_budget). The clause "it is not necessary to the formal principal theorem's contradiction" describes the Lean development (software). The finite-horizon form with satisfiable hypotheses is the article's certificate_budget_general (used for disp/021).

items.anchor: Armijo then traps all accepted iterates in $U$. This produces a local basin independent of $H_0$.
items.note: With lines 174-176 (the setting of disp/022): certificates only on K ∩ U (HasBandCertificates F (K ∩ U) F_* c₁ c₂), unique minimizer x_*, b > F_*. Then ∃ δ > 0 (chosen before the run, so independent of H_0) such that every admissible run with the constants c₁, c₂ and F(x_0) ≤ F_* + δ stays in K ∩ U, F(x_k) → F_*, x_k → x_*.

items.anchor: Rejected trial points need not stay in $U$.
items.note: Example: F(x) = x²/2 on R, U = {|x| < 1}, x_0 = 1/2, H_0 = 4: the unit trial point x_0 - H_0∇F(x_0) = -3/2 ∉ U violates Armijo for every 0 < c₁ < 1 (rejected), while the step α = 1/8 gives 1/4 ∈ U satisfying Armijo for c₁ ≤ 3/4. The run model itself has no trial points; the local basin (prose/022) concerns accepted iterates only.

items.anchor: For multiple minimizers, one may instead use a neighborhood of the entire compact solution set or directly assume that the initial sublevel lies in the structural region.
items.note: (a) solution_set_basin: U a neighborhood of every minimizer, certificates on {F ≤ b} ∩ U ({F ≤ b} compact, b > F_*): a basin F(x_0) ≤ F_* + δ for the fixed constants, iterates stay in {F ≤ b} ∩ U, F(x_k) → F_*, dist(x_k, argmin F) → 0. (b) structural_region_convergence: certificates on a region S containing the compact initial sublevel {F ≤ F(x_0)}: value and distance convergence (iterates for a unique minimizer).

items.anchor: The proof only needs a certificate in a small one-sided level neighborhood of each possible finite limit
items.note: HasShellCertificates F K F_* c₁ c₂: for every ℓ > F_* such that some x ∈ K has F(x) ≥ ℓ, ∃ ε_ℓ > 0 and a certificate on K ∩ {F ≤ ℓ + ε_ℓ} at level η = ℓ - F_*, whose band is the shell {x ∈ K : ℓ ≤ F(x) ≤ ℓ + ε_ℓ} (shell_band_eq). Whole-band certificates imply shell certificates (shell_certificates: "a cleaner, stronger formulation"), and shell certificates suffice (shell_convergence: value, Euclidean distance and unique-minimizer conclusions for runs starting in the compact K = {F ≤ b}).

items.anchor: there is no requirement that $\lambda$ be invertible or bounded away from zero.
items.note: The sufficient condition of disp/023 asks only |λ|² ≤ 1 + Ld; rank_one_degenerate states the case λ = 0 (v(z) = βs) explicitly, and degenerate_multiplier gives vectors (v(x) = e₁, s = e₂, v(z) = e₂ in R²) for which every decomposition v(z) = λv(x) + βs has λ = 0 while (T) holds for W = vvᵀ with L = 0. The opening contrast of the sentence ("Unlike the moving-frame criterion of Section~\ref{M:energy},", before its correction of 15 October 2026 "Unlike the preceding moving-frame theorem,") is item prose/043 (M26).

items.anchor: The PSD form also accommodates multiple comparison directions and varying rank, without choosing an exact frame transport.
items.note: The sum of two certificates on one band (e.g. of several rank-one fields, or of fields of different ranks) is a certificate with m = m₁ + m₂, C = C₁ + C₂, L = max, δ = min (certificate_sum); the definition (bandCertificate_iff) imposes no rank condition, and transport is only the Loewner inequality (T), not an exact frame relation V_{k+1} = V_kT_k + s_kb_kᵀ as in Chapter M.

items.anchor: A bounded potential may be absorbed into $W$.
items.note: Hypothesis: PotentialBandCertificate (field W with PSD, (V), (S) as in theorem/001, a potential Ψ with ψ_lo ≤ Ψ ≤ ψ_hi on the band, and (T) with multiplier exp{Ld + Ψ(x) - Ψ(z)}, display disp/025). Conclusions: (T) holds for e^Ψ W with multiplier exactly e^{Ld}; e^{Ld} ≤ 1 + 2Ld for 0 ≤ d ≤ 1/(L + 1) (L' = 2L); e^Ψ W is a band certificate with m' = e^{ψ_lo}m, C' = e^{ψ_hi}max{C, 0}, L' = 2L, δ' = min{δ, 1/(L + 1)} (band-dependent constants).

items.anchor: With this $W$, (S) is the inequality of (RS) restricted to eligible pairs in $K_\eta$ with $d\le\delta_\eta$, so (RS) gives (S) with the same constant
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M24): "Condition (S) is exactly (RS), while" now reads "With this $W$, (S) is the inequality of (RS) restricted to eligible pairs in $K_\eta$ with $d\le\delta_\eta$, so (RS) gives (S) with the same constant, while". For W(z) = (z - x_*)(z - x_*)ᵀ, yᵀW(z)y = N² and t = T, and every eligible pair x, z ∈ K_η (0 < c₁, c₂ < 1) satisfies the premises of (RS) (radial_secant_exact), so (RS) gives (S) with the same constant (rs_gives_s); s_not_exactly_rs shows that (S) does not give (RS). The rest of the sentence (prose/030, disp/028) and the conclusion of line 229 (prose/031) hold. Wording point W18 (applied the same day) gives (RS) a pointer to Chapter 4 at line 217.

items.anchor: makes (T) an equality with $L=0$
items.note: Π_sW(z)Π_s = Π_sW(x)Π_s for the radial field and s = z - x, so (T) holds with L = 0.

items.anchor: Thus every objective covered by RS is covered by the new condition.
items.note: Finite convex F with minimizer x_* and (RS) on K (HasRadialSecantBounds, C_η real): for all 0 < c₁, c₂ < 1 and η > 0 there is a band certificate with W = (x - x_*)(x - x_*)ᵀ, m = η², L = 0; hence HasBandCertificates F K F_* c₁ c₂ and theorem/001 applies.

items.anchor: The reverse implication fails.
items.note: With the next sentence ("Chapter Q constructs fields satisfying the new condition for a multi-branch curved objective that violates even the eligible-pair radial condition on every positive neighborhood of its minimizer"). Witness: F(u,v) = max{u² + v, 3u², 2u² - v} (Chapter Q, (10.18)): convex, unique minimizer 0, F(0) = 0, compact sublevels, band certificates on every compact set for all 0 < c₁, c₂ < 1 (the field (10.8)); on every neighborhood K of 0, (RS) fails, and for every fixed 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1 there is η > 0 such that eligible pairs in K with F(z) ≥ η, F(z) ≤ F(x) and arbitrarily small d beat every proposed bound N² ≤ Ct. "every positive neighborhood" is read as: every neighborhood of the minimizer, on a positive band.

items.anchor: This is strict inclusion of sufficient conditions, not merely a new notation for the old inequality.
items.note: Combines the inclusion (prose/031) and the failure of the reverse inclusion (prose/032).

items.anchor: Under an invertible affine change of variables with linear part $A$
items.note: For det A ≠ 0, z = Ax + b, F̃(z) = F(A⁻¹(z - b)): gradients become A^{-T}g at Ax + b; eligibility is preserved exactly; each band certificate of F on K gives one of F̃ on the image of K with W̃(Ax + b) = AW(x)Aᵀ and the same m, C, L, δ; existence of the certificates is equivalent ("the three conditions are affine-covariant").

items.anchor: The extra transport clause cannot simply be omitted
items.note: With the sentence "A small Euclidean change is not by itself a small change in the B_k energy": SPD B_k = diag(1, (k+1)⁴) (unbounded, B_k(1,1) → ∞) and v_k → v with vᵀB_kv = 1 but v_kᵀB_kv_k - vᵀB_kv → ∞. An algebraic example, not a BFGS trajectory; the first clause ("cannot simply be omitted") explains why the proof needs (T) rather than claiming that the theorem fails without it.

items.anchor: Projection and the multiplicative budget are precisely what make the new hypothesis sufficient without assumptions on $B_k$.
items.note: Summary of the proof mechanism: M_k = Π_{s_k}M_kΠ_{s_k} (disp/016) lets (T) be projected, and the multiplicative factor a_k = 1 + Ld_k in (3.6) (disp/019) is absorbed by the normalization; theorem/001 has no hypothesis on B_k.

items.anchor: The following comparisons are bibliographic scholarship, separate from the formal theorem assertions.
items.reason: Editorial statement about the section "Relation to earlier work".

items.anchor: This is a sufficient condition for ordinary full BFGS.
items.note: Theorem/001 states that the certificate condition is sufficient for convergence of every admissible (ordinary full BFGS) run.

items.anchor: Multiplicative-error normalization is an established technique
items.reason: Literature attribution (Combettes–Vũ, Lemmas 2.2–2.3) and cross-reference; the normalization used in this chapter is proved in Lean (disp/020, disp/021, prose/028).

items.anchor: The comparison field here may be singular and unbounded, and transport is projected away from the step.
items.note: Remark on the hypotheses of theorem/001: W only PSD (singular allowed, e.g. the rank-one fields of disp/023 and prose/031) and finite-valued with no bound; (T) involves Π_s only.

items.anchor: Consequently a uniformly coercive, bounded variable-metric convergence theorem does not supply this result or its objective-pair quantifiers.
items.reason: Comparison with the literature (variable-metric convergence theorems with uniformly bounded and coercive metrics); no mathematical claim about this chapter beyond prose/040.

items.anchor: Using (3.3)--(3.4), the Loewner inequality (T), and (S),
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M25): the three references of the proof now print (3.3)--(3.4) (line 148), (3.6) (line 160, "Divide (3.6) by $P_{k+1}$ and sum") and (3.5) (line 165, "This contradicts (3.5)."); before "(3)--(4)", "(6)" and "(5)", numbers that the companion does not print. The lead-in of display disp/019 (trace_recurrence) uses the Hessian form (3.3) (hessian_form) and the annihilation (3.4) (annihilation_projection); dividing (3.6) and summing is reciprocal_budget, and the contradiction is with (3.5) (reciprocal_mean_diverges), proving one_sided_convergence.

items.anchor: Unlike the moving-frame criterion of Section~\ref{M:energy},
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M26): "Unlike the preceding moving-frame theorem," now reads "Unlike the moving-frame criterion of Section~\ref{M:energy}," (Section 2.4). That criterion (02_M.tex:196-211, Ch02M.frame_criterion) assumes cumulative products P_{k+1} = P_kT_k with bounded norms and bounded inverse norms; the scalar sufficient condition of this chapter allows λ = 0 (rank_one_degenerate), also where λ = 0 is forced (degenerate_multiplier). Theorem M:residualtheorem, the literal referent before the correction, requires no invertible transport either (Ch02M.residual_theorem).

items.anchor: imposing a condition on all such pairs is an objective-only sufficient assumption
items.note: The conditions of theorem/001 are imposed on all eligible pairs, and EligiblePair F c₁ c₂ x z g h is defined from F and the line-search constants alone (objective-only); every accepted step is eligible (prose/006), so such a condition constrains every run, and theorem/001 shows that the certificate condition suffices for convergence. Sufficient, not necessary: the article's certificate_not_necessary.

resolved_discrepancies.description: "Condition (S) is exactly (RS), while" (03_T.tex:225). With W(x) = (x - x_*)(x - x_*)^T, the (S) inequality y^T W(z) y <= C_eta t is the (RS) inequality N^2 <= C_eta T (y^T W(z) y = (y^T (z - x_*))^2 = N^2 and t = T), but (S) is required only for eligible pairs x, z in K_eta with d <= delta_eta (03_T.tex:106), whereas (RS) (04_R.tex:53-59) quantifies over all differentiable x, z in K with F_* + eta <= F(z) <= F(x) and T > 0. Every eligible pair in K_eta satisfies these premises, so (RS) gives (S) with the same constant (rs_gives_s, radial_secant_exact) and the inclusion drawn at line 229 holds (rs_covered); the converse fails. For F(x) = max(|x|, 2x - 1) on R (finite, convex, unique minimizer 0, K = {F <= 2} compact) and every c_2 < 1/2, (S) holds for the radial field with C_eta = 6 on every band, for every eligible pair, and the radial field is a band certificate (m = eta^2, C = 6, L = 0, delta = 1), yet (RS) fails on K: at eta = 1/2 the pairs x = 1 + eps, z = 1 - eps have N^2/T = (1 - eps)^2/(2 eps) -> infinity; they have t = d/2 < (1 - c_2) d, so they are not eligible (s_not_exactly_rs). The companion itself separates (RS) from its eligible-pair restriction (03_T.tex:231, "violates even the eligible-pair radial condition"; 10_Q.tex:300).

resolved_discrepancies.description: The proof of the theorem cites its equations by the short numbers of the source: "Using (3)--(4), the Loewner inequality (T), and (S)," (03_T.tex:148) means (3.3)-(3.4) (the Hessian update, and M_k s_k = 0, M_k = Pi_{s_k} M_k Pi_{s_k}); "Divide (6) by $P_{k+1}$ and sum" (line 160) means the trace recurrence (3.6); "This contradicts (5)." (line 165) means the divergence (3.5). The source (bfgs_lean_stage1/master_report/latex/chapters/T.tex:134, 146, 151) tags these equations (T.3)-(T.6) but cites them without the prefix, and editorial/generate_companion.py:69 renames only prefixed numbers (T.3 -> 3.3), so the companion prints "(3)--(4)", "(6)" and "(5)", numbers that exist nowhere in it (Chapter 3 tags (3.2), (3.V), (3.S), (3.T), (3.3)-(3.6); companion/build/master.pdf, PDF page 23 = printed page 17). The mathematics holds with the intended references: hessian_form (3.3), annihilation_projection (3.4), trace_recurrence (3.6), reciprocal_budget (dividing (3.6) and summing), reciprocal_mean_diverges (3.5), one_sided_convergence (the theorem that the contradiction proves).
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: Print "(3.3)--(3.4)" (line 148), "(3.6)" (line 160) and "(3.5)" (line 165): logged module-T replacements in editorial/generate_companion.py of "Using (3)--(4)," by "Using (3.3)--(3.4),", "Divide (6) by" by "Divide (3.6) by" and "This contradicts (5)." by "This contradicts (3.5)." (source T.tex:134, 146, 151, one occurrence each).

resolved_discrepancies.description: "Unlike the preceding moving-frame theorem, there is no requirement that $\lambda$ be invertible or bounded away from zero." (03_T.tex:196). The only moving-frame theorem before Chapter 3 is Theorem M:residualtheorem (Residuals in fixed smooth directions, 02_M.tex:220-237), and it requires no invertible transport either (02_M.tex:236: "No full-rank frame or invertible transport is required."; Ch02M.residual_theorem assumes only ||T_k||_op^2 <= 1 + C_T d_k), so the contrast is false for the literal referent. The intended referent is the moving-frame criterion stated in prose in Section 2.4 (02_M.tex:196-211, summarized as result P2 at 01_I.tex:159-161), which assumes that the cumulative products P_{k+1} = P_k T_k have bounded norms and bounded inverse norms (Ch02M.frame_criterion, hypotheses hPinv and hPinvbdd); in the scalar case every lambda_k is then nonzero and the products stay away from zero. What the sentence says of Chapter 3 holds: its scalar sufficient condition v(z) = lambda v(x) + beta s, |lambda|^2 <= 1 + L d allows lambda = 0 (rank_one_degenerate), also where lambda = 0 is forced (degenerate_multiplier). Same policy as C/05_G/prose/008.
